note.text: Bank-related language includes account, deposit, withdrawal and balance. Their meanings depend on the stated transaction and perspective. An abbreviation shortens a longer expression and should be expanded before use if its meaning is unfamiliar. Do not assume that every institution uses the same forms or charges. This is a fictional vocabulary exercise, not an instruction to open an account or a statement of current banking rules.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Bank-related language includes account, deposit, withdrawal and balance. Their meanings depend on the stated transaction and perspective. sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original notice: An imaginary school savings exercise records a deposit as money added and a withdrawal as money taken out. The balance records the amount remaining in the model account at that point. The label ATM expands to automated teller machine. The passage does not give permission to use another person's card or request real personal banking details.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Read from the account holder's stated perspective and check whether a movement adds or removes money. Expand an unfamiliar abbreviation from an appropriate source. Never infer a real fee, interest rate or account condition from a classroom example.
